clue.text: Channel Islands property with a set of rules and regulations

parts.note: a villa is a property, a country house

explanation.surface: A Jersey or Guernsey estate comes with its own rulebook.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil law is a body of legal rules governing private matters between citizens, a system of regulations.

clue.text: Worshipper's tailored pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the word beside it is badly made and rearranged

explanation.surface: A devotee wears smart made-to-measure trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is the British slang for rubbish, signalling the rearrangement; 'tailored' is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: One who worships images or false gods; the 's stands for is.

clue.text: Aware where star may be seen?

definitions.meaning: kept informed, knowing what is going on
a film star appears on screen, in a movie

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fully informed; literally it is where a film actor appears, within a movie.

clue.text: Smith, say, after all is on call?

parts.note: last means after all the others
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A blacksmith is on duty when everyone else has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smith' looks like a craftsman but is an example of a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Smith is a common example of a surname or family name.

clue.text: Flush with success? The opposite

parts.note: flush with success means brimming with triumph; its opposite is an utter failure, and flushing also suggests rinsing water

explanation.surface: Someone flush with success, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flush' hints at water rinsing things away, which the answer's literal sense also suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete failure or fiasco, something rained off: the reverse of a triumph.

clue.text: Cold milk served up? Puss would like that

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: in a down entry served up means presented upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk, from an old advertising slogan

explanation.surface: A saucer of chilled milk set out for the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puss would like that' looks like a comment on the milk but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb whose scent strongly attracts and excites cats, hence its common name.

clue.text: Pop round to see what's above the skirting board

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Father nips over to inspect the wall decor.
explanation.walkthrough: A skirting board runs along the bottom of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of an interior wall, panelled or decorated, between skirting and rail.

clue.text: Killer naturally hated being injured by explosive

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters of hated are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: a cap is a small explosive charge, as in a toy cap gun

explanation.surface: A murderer, of course, loathes being hurt by a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: This poisonous mushroom is a natural killer, the most lethal fungus found in the wild.

clue.text: Water in a valley almost disappearing on a regular basis

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, as in the Yorkshire Dales

indicators.note: every other letter of almost vanishes, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A stream in a valley dries up now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like the stream in the valley but is the definition; 'disappearing on a regular basis' works on the word 'almost', not on the water, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for plain drinking water, the only drink the first man had.

clue.text: Recalled extract from what followed Room At The Top

indicators.note: Recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Recalling a passage from the sequel to the novel Room at the Top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room At The Top' is the John Braine novel title in the surface; read literally it is the definition. 'extract from' gives TFOL inside wHAT FOLlowed and 'Recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic space directly under the roof is literally the room at the top of a house.

clue.text: Job for the registrar, perhaps, where groom might tie the knot

definitions.meaning: a registrar's post or job is marrying couples, getting them hitched

definitions.text: where groom might tie the knot
definitions.meaning: a stable groom ties a horse's rein to a post with a knot

explanation.surface: A wedding official's task is where the bridegroom gets married.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves trade on 'groom' and 'tie the knot': the bridegroom marrying, or a stable lad tethering a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A post to tether horses, and punningly a registrar's position of getting people hitched.

clue.text: News announcement: relief after squeeze on pound

indicators.note: after places relief behind the other pieces

parts.note: to squeeze is to press
RE means on or concerning, as in business letters
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from libra
relief from pain is ease

explanation.surface: Headline: relief follows a squeeze on sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'relief' as the whole second word leaves 'on pound' unexplained; 'on' and 'pound' are small pieces of their own, and 'after' puts relief at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement issued to journalists by an organisation, officially announcing news.

clue.text: Splashing out, I'll visit US state: the perfect place to be

indicators.note: splashing out scatters the letters of out into a new order
to visit is to go inside, so I goes within the state abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania
I'll is I will: the letter I is the one doing the visiting

explanation.surface: A spendthrift plans a lavish trip to an American state they consider paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splashing out' reads as spending freely, but 'Splashing' alone is the anagram signal with 'out' its material; 'visit' is the container signal for I'll's I.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia, from Thomas More's book, is an imagined ideal society, the perfect place.

clue.text: Name work Greek character rejected as prosaic

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the three pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to name someone, as a source or in court, is to cite them
OP is short for opus, a musical work
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A writer's work about a Greek figure is turned down as dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic writing lacks poetry and imagination, so it is unpoetic in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Tube announcement of line closure in Aldgate area

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word for line is heard rather than written

parts.note: a railway line is a track

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter, taken from each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A London Underground notice about a line being shut near Aldgate, a station in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' is the London Underground in the surface but the windpipe here. 'closure in' gives E and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is a tube carrying air from larynx to lungs, its anatomical name.

clue.text: American political group still on the rise, though split internally

indicators.note: internally puts the split inside the reversed word
in a down entry rising means read upwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: still means yet, as in not finished yet
split means apart, separated

explanation.surface: A US party gaining support despite internal divisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns YET into TEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservative US political movement, named after the Boston protest of 1773.

clue.text: Granulated sugar's first off pallet for shop

indicators.note: granulated means broken into grains, so the letters are crumbled and rearranged

parts.note: sugar's read as sugars, giving its letters with the S

indicators.note: the first letter off pallet is taken

explanation.surface: Bags of granulated sugar are the first goods unloaded from a pallet for the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is a verb: to inform on someone. 'Granulated' rearranges SUGARS plus P.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to shop someone to the police is to betray them, to inform on them.

clue.text: Servicemen safe when carrying a firearm

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the safe holds the A

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Soldiers keep a weapon safely locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle or pistol that fires several shots without reloading is a repeating firearm.

clue.text: World Service grabs minister during uprising

indicators.note: grabs means seizes and holds inside

parts.note: use is service, as in being of service

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising reads upwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister
in means during

explanation.surface: The BBC World Service reports a minister caught up in a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'World Service' looks like the BBC's overseas radio broadcaster; split, 'World' is the definition. 'uprising' turns REVIN into NIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is everything that exists, the whole world in its widest sense.

clue.text: Advantages of technology to support head of faculty

indicators.note: in a down entry supporting means sitting beneath, so this piece goes below

parts.note: a professor, prof for short, heads a university faculty
IT is information technology, so its means of IT

explanation.surface: The benefits of using technology to back up a university dean.
explanation.definitionFit: Profits are gains or benefits, the advantages one derives from something.

clue.text: One makes tiny reforms fairer with backing of attorney

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the attorney's letters run backwards

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, the American public prosecutor
fairer means more just

explanation.surface: A reformer improves the law slightly with a lawyer's support.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes small changes and fine corrections to something is one who tweaks or adjusts it.

clue.text: Subsequently graduate's assimilated Ancient Greek

indicators.note: assimilated means absorbed, so the graduate goes within

parts.note: subsequently means then, afterwards
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Later a graduate absorbed the classical languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Thebes, a leading city-state of classical Greece.

clue.text: Facing pressure, runner suffers setback in early round of contest

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the runner's letters are reversed

parts.note: a miler is an athlete who runs the mile

explanation.surface: An athlete under pressure falters in the heats.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for preliminary, a qualifying stage held before the main rounds of a competition.

clue.text: Not much to eat, but enough for a picnic?

definitions.meaning: a single slice of a sponge is only a small snack
a picnic, informally, is something very easy to do

explanation.surface: A modest snack that would still do for an outdoor meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very easy task, as is 'a picnic'; literally it is a single slice of a sponge.

clue.text: Fellow first out of bed

indicators.note: first out of means the opening letter leaves the word for bed

parts.note: a divan is a type of bed

explanation.surface: A man is the first to get up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a common Russian man's name, so a typical fellow or chap, one man.

clue.text: About end of dinner one's given port

indicators.note: about means around, so the ace goes round the picked letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards; the 's is is

indicators.note: the end of dinner is its final letter

explanation.surface: Towards the close of a dinner each guest is handed a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is the fortified wine in the surface but a harbour town here: Acre in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre (Akko) is an ancient harbour city on the coast of northern Israel.

clue.text: Do leaders of thieves temporarily stash away most of loot?

indicators.note: to stash something away is to put it inside, here between the leading letters
the leaders of the next two words are their first letters
most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: to loot a place is to ransack it

explanation.surface: Do burglars temporarily hide most of the stolen goods?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the start of a question but is the definition. 'most of' cuts RANSACK to RANSAC.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out, to do a deal.

clue.text: Carefully checked points put in writing

indicators.note: put in places the compass points inside the word for writing

parts.note: a screed is a long piece of writing
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: Notes made after carefully checking some points of argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Screened candidates or patients have been vetted, examined and tested for problems.
